[LLM] AGENTPSD-style Python reverse shell spawned by sshd on Linux / NAS Installation Medium
Hunts the AGENTPSD deployment pattern Volexity describes: VerdantBamboo SSHed into Synology NAS / Linux appliances and dropped a Python-based reverse shell. Surfaces python3 / python processes whose parent is sshd and which subsequently open an outbound socket — a behaviour pattern that survives even when the static hashes mutate. Rationale: The article specifically calls out AGENTPSD as a Python reverse shell deployed over SSH to the Synology NAS. Parent=sshd + child=python is a tight behavioural pair on appliances where Python is rarely launched interactively; the cmd-line tokens are the canonical Python reverse-shell idioms. Cross-checked Volexity blog for the deployment vector (SSH). Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/chinese-apt-verdantbamboo-uses-brickstorm-malware/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1021.004 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName == "sshd"
| where FileName in~ ("python","python2","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("socket.", "subprocess.", "pty.spawn", "os.dup2", "-c import", "connect((", "/bin/sh", "/bin/bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "sshd"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/python(2|3)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("socket.", "subprocess.", "pty.spawn", "os.dup2", "-c import", "connect((", "/bin/sh", "/bin/bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
title: AGENTPSD-style Python Reverse Shell Spawned by sshd
id: a4127bc8-c5b6-4e5e-b1ec-3f7d4f7c4d31
description: Detects a python interpreter spawned directly by sshd on a Linux / BSD host with command-line arguments matching reverse-shell semantics (socket import, pty.spawn, os.dup2, connect to /bin/sh). Maps to the VerdantBamboo AGENTPSD deployment pattern Volexity documented (June 2026).
references:
  - https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1021.004
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '/sshd'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python2'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'socket.'
      - 'pty.spawn'
      - 'os.dup2'
      - 'subprocess.'
      - '-c import'
      - '/bin/sh'
      - '/bin/bash'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:sshd @process.name:(python OR python2 OR python3) @process.command_line:(*socket.* OR *pty.spawn* OR *os.dup2* OR *subprocess.* OR *"/bin/sh"* OR *"/bin/bash"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 #event_platform=Lin
| ParentBaseFileName=/^sshd$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/python(2|3)?$/i
| regex("(socket\.|pty\.spawn|os\.dup2|subprocess\.|-c import|\/bin\/sh|\/bin\/bash)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Outbound endpoint connections to BRICKSTORM C2 IP 149.248.11.71 Command & Control High
Catches any endpoint, server or appliance making an outbound network connection to the VerdantBamboo BRICKSTORM C2 address. Distinct pivot from UC1 (M365 sign-ins) — this targets the BRICKSTORM SOCKS callback channel rather than the resulting Entra session, so it fires even if the proxy never reaches a successful sign-in. Rationale: 149.248.11.71 is the only network-layer IOC Volexity published. The detection covers every host that BRICKSTORM might call out from (Storage Sync, pfSense, Synology NAS, Windows endpoints) by hitting both EDR and firewall telemetry. Cross-checked Volexity, BleepingComputer and Mallory.ai. Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-apt-deploys-new-malware-to-keep-access-to-hacked-networks/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "149.248.11.71"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "149.248.11.71"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcAction, SrcUsername),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP == "149.248.11.71"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceAction, SourceUserName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] pfSense / firewall config change enabling Web SSL VPN after admin login Installation Medium
Hunts the VerdantBamboo re-entry tactic Volexity documents — after stolen admin credentials let them into the firewall, the actor enabled web SSL VPN access to the appliance and used it for ongoing entry. Surfaces config-write events on the firewall WebGUI / SSL VPN service originating from previously-unseen admin source IPs, correlated to a successful admin login in the preceding 15 minutes. Rationale: Volexity explicitly describes the actor reconnecting to the firewall with stolen admin credentials and then enabling web SSL VPN access on the device — Syslog/php-fpm/configd messages on pfSense are the canonical witness for that change. Defender / Falcon are left empty because pfSense appliances are not typically EDR-instrumented; Sigma is left empty because the correlation requires a time-window join between two log events (rule explicitly forbidden for single-event-shape Sigma). Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/06/04/verdantbamboo-just-another-brickstorm-in-the-firewall/ • https://cyberpress.org/verdantbamboo-breaches-pfsense-firewall/
ATT&CKT1556 T1133 T1078
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let AdminLogins = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv") or ProcessName in ("sshd","webConfigurator","php-fpm")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("Successful login for user 'admin'", "Successful webConfigurator login", "Accepted password for admin")
    | extend AdminIP = extract(@"from ([\d\.]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | project AdminLoginTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, AdminIP;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ProcessName in ("php-fpm","configd","check_reload_status","openvpn")

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has

// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-22769")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child

level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'

level: critical

The Hades Campaign: Graph ML PyPI Packages Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers, AI Analyst Misdirection, and a Wiper Deterrent

StepSecurity
2026-06-08 13 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On June 8, 2026, multiple Graph ML PyPI packages in the bioinformatics ecosystem were compromised in the Hades campaign, deploying cross-platform memory scrapers, AI prompt injections to misdirect scanners, and a token-revocation wiper.

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The Hades Campaign: Graph ML PyPI Packages Deploy Cross-Platform Memory Scrapers
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Hades Campaign python import hook spawning bun runtime from /tmp · [LLM] Hades Campaign persistence artifacts (systemd units + updater.py + lock/state files) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Hades Campaign GitHub commit-search C2 with firedalazer / DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom markers · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scrape of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Hades Campaign PyPI install of compromised graph-ML / bio package versions Delivery High
Detects pip/uv/poetry installation or on-disk arrival of the exact seven Hades Campaign package@version pairs (ensmallen 0.8.101, embiggen 0.11.97, gpsea 0.9.14, pyphetools 0.9.120, mflux-streamlit 0.0.3-0.0.4, nhmpy 2.4.7, ppkt2synergy 0.1.1). Catches the supply-chain compromise at the moment it lands on a developer or CI host, before the __init__.py import hook is ever triggered. Rationale: Pivots on the exact seven package@version pairs listed in the article's affected-versions table plus the .dist-info folder names pip writes to site-packages — every legitimate developer/CI install of these versions IS the compromise, so confidence is high. Dual surfaces (process exec AND file creation) catch out-of-band installs (uv lock, poetry, wheel cache copy).
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

let HadesDistInfo = dynamic(["ensmallen-0.8.101.dist-info","embiggen-0.11.97.dist-info","gpsea-0.9.14.dist-info","pyphetools-0.9.120.dist-info","mflux_streamlit-0.0.3.dist-info","mflux_streamlit-0.0.4.dist-info","nhmpy-2.4.7.dist-info","ppkt2synergy-0.1.1.dist-info"]);
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where FileName in~ ("pip","pip.exe","pip3","pip3.exe","uv","uv.exe","poetry","poetry.exe") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip.exe","pip3","pip3.exe")
 | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Surface="process", FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
 | where FolderPath has_any (HadesDistInfo) or FileName has_any (HadesPkgVersions)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Surface="file", FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine="", FolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let HadesPkgVersions = dynamic(["ensmallen==0.8.101","ensmallen-0.8.101","embiggen==0.11.97","embiggen-0.11.97","gpsea==0.9.14","gpsea-0.9.14","pyphetools==0.9.120","pyphetools-0.9.120","mflux-streamlit==0.0.3","mflux-streamlit==0.0.4","mflux_streamlit-0.0.3","mflux_streamlit-0.0.4","nhmpy==2.4.7","nhmpy-2.4.7","ppkt2synergy==0.1.1","ppkt2synergy-0.1.1"]);

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","uv","poetry") or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","uv","poetry")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgVersions)

[LLM] Hades Campaign python import hook spawning bun runtime from /tmp Installation High
Detects the Hades Campaign __init__.py import-hook execution chain: a python interpreter spawning the Bun runtime out of /tmp/b/bun (or its zip extraction) running `_index.js`. This is the moment the malicious payload actually executes after package import, on Linux/macOS/Windows runners and developer hosts. Rationale: Bun is not a stock Linux/macOS/Windows binary and an out-of-tree path like `/tmp/b/bun` being launched by a python interpreter is the article's exact described chain (`_s.run([_b, "run", _j], ...)` in the deobfuscated import hook). Pairing parent=python with image=bun and a `/tmp/b/` or `_index.js` predicate is essentially the campaign signature with near-zero legitimate overlap.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.007 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "python"
| where (FileName =~ "bun" or FileName =~ "bun.exe")
      or FolderPath has_any (@"/tmp/b/", @"\Temp\b\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\b\")
      or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", @"\Temp\b\bun", "_index.js")
| extend BunPath = FolderPath, BunCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, BunPath, BunCmd,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "python" or ActingProcessName has "python"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
      or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", @"\Temp\b\bun", "_index.js")
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/b/bun", "_index.js")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Hades Campaign persistence artifacts (systemd units + updater.py + lock/state files) Installation High
Detects creation of the Hades Campaign on-disk persistence indicators: systemd user units update-monitor.service / gh-token-monitor.service, the C2 polling script updater.py under ~/.local/share/updater/, and the lock/state markers /tmp/.bun_ran, /tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock, /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. Any one of these on a non-detonation host is a high-fidelity indicator of active infection. Rationale: Every path here is verbatim from the article's IOC table or kill-chain block — `~/.local/share/updater/update.py`, `~/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service`, `~/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service`, `/tmp/.bun_ran`, `/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock`, `/var/tmp/.gh_update_state`. The chance of an unrelated legitimate process writing this exact combination of paths is essentially zero — the systemd-unit + lockfile pair alone is conclusive.
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let HadesFiles = dynamic(["update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state","tmp.0144018410.lock"]);

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName in (HadesFiles)
      or FolderPath has_any (HadesPaths)
      or (FolderPath has "/.local/share/updater" and FileName =~ "update.py")
      or (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName has_any ("update-monitor","gh-token-monitor"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileCreate","FileWrite","FileRename","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName in ("update-monitor.service","gh-token-monitor.service",".bun_ran",".gh_update_state","tmp.0144018410.lock","update.py","updater.py")
      or TargetFilePath has_any ("/.config/systemd/user/update-monitor.service","/.config/systemd/user/gh-token-monitor.service","/.local/share/updater/","/tmp/.bun_ran","/tmp/tmp.0144018410.lock","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
| where not (TargetFileName =~ "update.py" and not(TargetFilePath has "/.local/share/updater"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Hades Campaign GitHub commit-search C2 with firedalazer / DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom markers Command & Control High
Detects the three independent GitHub-as-C2 channels used by the Hades Campaign: outbound traffic or process command lines referencing api.github.com/search/commits combined with the magic strings `firedalazer`, `DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, or `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`. These markers are the dead-drop discriminators the malware searches GitHub for to retrieve new payloads, token-revocation status, and exfil-destination repos. Rationale: The three magic strings (`firedalazer`, `DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`) are quoted verbatim in the kill-chain reconstruction as the attacker-controlled discriminators searched for via api.github.com/search/commits — they are unique enough that a single hit in URL or process command-line is high-confidence. Multi-surface (network + process) catches the malware whether the request leaves the host (network) or is logged by AMSI/script telemetry (process).
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web Endpoint.Processes
let HadesMarkers = dynamic(["firedalazer","DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesMarkers) or RemoteUrl has "search/commits"
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Surface="network", RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName),
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
 | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Surface="process", RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl="",
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine," | child=",ProcessCommandLine), InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc

(CommonSecurityLog

 | where DestinationHostName has "api.github.com" or RequestURL has "api.github.com"
 | where RequestURL has_any (HadesMarkers) or Message has_any (HadesMarkers)
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor),
(ImWebSession

 | where Url has_any (HadesMarkers)

(ImProcessCreate

 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=DvcIpAddr, SourceUserName=ActorUsername, DestinationHostName="process", RequestURL=TargetProcessCommandLine, DeviceVendor=EventVendor)

[LLM] Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scrape of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the article's tailored Linux/macOS/Windows memory-read primitives against the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process: a non-runner parent (python, pwsh, bun, mshta) referencing `Runner.Worker`, `/proc/<pid>/mem`, `task_for_pid`, `mach_vm_read_overwrite`, `ReadProcessMemory`, or `VirtualQueryEx` while a Runner.Worker process is co-resident on the host. Rationale: The article calls out the exact API surfaces per OS: `task_for_pid` + `mach_vm_read_overwrite` + `vm_region_basic_info_64` on macOS, `ReadProcessMemory`/`VirtualQueryEx`/`PROCESS_VM_READ` on Windows, and `/proc/<pid>/mem` + `/proc/<pid>/maps` on Linux — all targeting the `Runner.Worker` process specifically. Restricting to hosts where Runner.Worker actually exists kills FP from generic memory-debug tooling on non-CI machines, and limiting parents to python/pwsh/bun matches the Hades execution chain.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.001 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let MemPrimitives = dynamic(["Runner.Worker","task_for_pid","mach_vm_read_overwrite","vm_region_basic_info_64","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","PROCESS_VM_READ","/proc/","process_vm_readv"]);
let ScraperParents = dynamic(["python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe","python3.11","python3.12","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh","bun","bun.exe"]);
let RunnerHosts =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "Runner.Worker" or FileName =~ "Runner.Worker.exe" or ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker"
    | distinct DeviceId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (RunnerHosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (ScraperParents) or FileName has_any (ScraperParents)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MemPrimitives)
| where not(FileName =~ "Runner.Worker" or FileName =~ "Runner.Worker.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let MemPrimitives = dynamic(["Runner.Worker","task_for_pid","mach_vm_read_overwrite","vm_region_basic_info_64","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","PROCESS_VM_READ","/proc/","process_vm_readv"]);

| where ActingProcessName has_any (ScraperParents) or ParentProcessName has_any (ScraperParents) or TargetProcessName has_any (ScraperParents)

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Quick Assist launched followed by remote interactive session (UNC3753 vishing pretext) Delivery Medium
Detects users launching Microsoft Quick Assist (quickassist.exe) and then a remote-controlled session beginning shortly after — the UNC3753 pretext for IT-help-desk vishing. Article-specific because UNC3753 explicitly named Quick Assist alongside Zoom/Teams as the screen-share entry vector. Rationale: Article names Quick Assist explicitly as a vector. The binary is fairly rare in most enterprises (Teams/Zoom are more common), so plain execution is a hunt-grade pivot. Corroborated with CISA & Microsoft advisories on Storm-1811/Quick Assist abuse. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1566.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "quickassist.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "quickassist.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\quickassist.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\quickassist.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Quick Assist Execution (UNC3753 Vishing Pretext)
id: 6f2a8b3c-1c7d-4f50-a47b-2a3df9b1a401
description: Detects launch of Microsoft Quick Assist (quickassist.exe), abused by UNC3753/Luna Moth/SRG to obtain remote-control screen-share sessions after vishing IT-helpdesk pretexts.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unc3753-used-vishing-and-physical.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/08
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1566.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\quickassist.exe'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\quickassist.exe OR *\QuickAssist.exe OR *\QUICKASSIST.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\quickassist\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="quickassist.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="quickassist.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="quickassist.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="quickassist.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
[LLM] AnyDesk, Bomgar, SuperOps or Zoho Assist installer execution (UNC3753 RMM foothold) Installation Medium
Detects fresh installation or first-time execution of the specific RMM tools UNC3753 instructs vishing victims to install (AnyDesk, Bomgar, SuperOps RMM, Zoho Assist). High-value hunting pivot since the article names these four explicitly. Rationale: Article explicitly names these four RMM tools as the post-vishing foothold mechanism. None should be ubiquitous in an org with a single sanctioned RMM — flag the deviations. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-156a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1020/
ATT&CKT1219 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let RMMBinaries = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","bomgar-scc.exe","bomgarportal.exe","bomgar.exe","superops.rmm.agent.exe","superops_agent.exe","zohoassist.exe","zohomeeting.exe","za_connect.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ (RMMBinaries)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AnyDesk","Bomgar","SuperOps","Zoho Assist")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let RMMBinaries = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","bomgar-scc.exe","bomgarportal.exe","bomgar.exe","superops.rmm.agent.exe","superops_agent.exe","zohoassist.exe","zohomeeting.exe","za_connect.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcessFile = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcessFile in (RMMBinaries)
   or CommandLine has_any ("AnyDesk","Bomgar","SuperOps","Zoho Assist")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Privnote[.]com self-destructing-note URL access from corporate endpoint Delivery Medium
Detects users browsing to privnote.com — the legitimate self-destruct-note service UNC3753 uses to deliver RMM install instructions during vishing calls without leaving recoverable evidence. Article-specific: privnote was explicitly named as the delivery channel. Rationale: Privnote is a legitimate but rarely-business-justified service. Article calls it out as UNC3753's instruction-delivery mechanism — DNS / proxy visibility on it is a cheap, high-signal pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://krebsonsecurity.com/2023/05/phishing-domains-tanked-after-meta-sued-freenom/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/
ATT&CKT1102 T1566.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Resolution.DNS
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","mssense.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DnsQuery has "privnote.com"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WinSCP or Rclone exfiltration from end-user workstations Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects WinSCP and Rclone process execution from user-context endpoints — UNC3753's named exfiltration tooling for staged sensitive data. Filters out IT-admin and backup-team baseline use. Rationale: Article names WinSCP and Rclone as the staged-exfil tooling. Both binaries are extremely rare in finance/legal services user contexts. Strong hunt-grade signal when scoped away from backup/IT. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1040/ • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-061a
ATT&CKT1567 T1048
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("winscp.exe","winscp.com","rclone.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("rclone copy","rclone sync","rclone copyto","winscp.com /command","open sftp://","open ftps://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("backupsvc","sftpsvc"))
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("backup","jumpbox","bastion"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ProcessFile = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ProcessFile in ("winscp.exe","winscp.com","rclone.exe")
   or CommandLine has_any ("rclone copy","rclone sync","rclone copyto","winscp.com /command","open sftp://","open ftps://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (SubjectUserName has_any ("backupsvc","sftpsvc"))
| where not (Computer has_any ("backup","jumpbox","bastion"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] USB mass-storage attached followed by bulk file copy (UNC3753 physical intrusion) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects USB mass-storage attach events followed within 30 minutes by a high volume of file writes/reads against the device — modelling the FBI-reported UNC3753 escalation where threat actors enter offices in person posing as IT technicians and exfiltrate via external USB drives. Rationale: FBI advisory and the article both call out the new in-person USB-exfil escalation. Removable-media + bulk-write correlation on the user's workstation is the only telemetry surface for this physical-intrusion variant. Image [1] (vishing.jpg) reinforces the broader social-engineering pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ic3.gov/Media/News/2024/240712.pdf • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1052/001/
ATT&CKT1052.001 T1200
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let USBAttach = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("UsbDriveMounted","PnpDeviceConnected","UsbDriveDriveLetterChanged")
    | project AttachTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, AdditionalFields;
let BulkCopy = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
    | summarize FileCount = count(), FirstWrite=min(Timestamp), LastWrite=max(Timestamp), SampleFile=any(FolderPath) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
    | where FileCount > 50;
USBAttach
| join kind=inner BulkCopy on DeviceId
| where FirstWrite between (AttachTime .. AttachTime + 30m)
| project AttachTime, FirstWrite, LastWrite, DeviceName, AccountName, FileCount, SampleFile, AdditionalFields
| order by AttachTime desc
let USBAttach = Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventLog == "Microsoft-Windows-DriverFrameworks-UserMode/Operational"
       or (EventLog == "System" and EventID in (20001,20003))
    | project AttachTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID;
let BulkCopy = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4663
    | where ObjectName matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"
    | summarize FileCount = count(), FirstAccess=min(TimeGenerated), LastAccess=max(TimeGenerated), SampleFile=any(ObjectName) by Computer, AccountName=SubjectUserName
    | where FileCount > 50;
USBAttach
| join kind=inner BulkCopy on Computer
| where FirstAccess between (AttachTime .. AttachTime + 30m)
| project AttachTime, FirstAccess, LastAccess, Computer, AccountName, FileCount, SampleFile
| order by AttachTime desc
source:windows.security @EventID:6416 @ClassName:DiskDrive
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^[D-Z]:\\\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count(as=FileCount))
| FileCount > 50

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.file_path IN ("E:\\*","F:\\*","G:\\*","H:\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where count > 50 AND firstTime > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
[LLM] Outbound mail to or domain lookup of business-data-leaks[.]com (UNC3753 extortion infrastructure) Command & Control High
Detects communications with business-data-leaks.com — the UNC3753 / Luna Moth data-leak-site domain referenced in extortion follow-ups. Any DNS lookup or email contact with this domain from the enterprise indicates either an in-progress extortion or a curious researcher. Rationale: Domain explicitly referenced in the article (LEAKEDDATA leak site) and corroborated by Mandiant attribution. Hits should be near-zero in normal enterprise traffic. Image [2] (LEAKEDDATA.png) corroborates the leak-site branding. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1020/ • https://www.ic3.gov/Media/News/2024/240712.pdf
ATT&CKT1567 T1657
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Email.All_Email
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where RemoteUrl has "business-data-leaks.com" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents", InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
(EmailEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SenderFromAddress has "business-data-leaks.com" or SenderMailFromDomain has "business-data-leaks.com" | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", Source="EmailEvents", InitiatingProcessAccountName=RecipientEmailAddress, InitiatingProcessFileName=Subject, RemoteUrl=SenderFromAddress, RemoteIP="")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has "business-data-leaks.com" | project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery),
(OfficeActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Operation has_any ("Send","MailItemsAccessed") | where tostring(EventData) has "business-data-leaks.com" | project TimeGenerated, Source="Office365", SrcHostname="", SrcIpAddr=ClientIP, SrcUsername=UserId, Indicator="business-data-leaks.com")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
